clue.text: Chap about done with new mexico's legislature

indicators.note: the word for a chap is placed around the other pieces, so about signals a surround

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap
over means finished or done
M is Mexico in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man who has finished dealing with the new Mexican parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GENT around OVER, N and M; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The body that rules a country, its legislature and executive together, is called its administration in everyday speech.

clue.text: Government worried after year's spin

indicators.note: worried follows the year in the clue, so its word comes after YR in the answer

parts.note: YR is the usual abbreviation for year
ate in the sense 'what's eating you?' means troubled or worried

explanation.surface: Government anxious about the spin it has put on the year.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE for 'worried' comes from 'eat' meaning to trouble someone, as in 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to turn rapidly round a centre, the same motion as whirling in a circle.

clue.text: Active firm has opening for factory food producer

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of factory
active suggests the letters of firm and has busily moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A busy company has a vacancy for a factory food maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening for' gives F, the first letter of 'factory'; 'Active' rearranges FIRM and HAS into ISHFARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that breeds and rears fish for the table is a supplier of food.

clue.text: Right line carried by Public Relations

indicators.note: the line is carried inside the abbreviation, so the second piece holds the first

parts.note: a rope is a line, as on a ship

explanation.surface: The correct message was conveyed by the PR department.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting, as right does in 'the right way to behave'.

clue.text: Painting animals dancing round ring

indicators.note: the rearranged animals go round the ring, enclosing it
dancing letters jump about, so animals is rearranged

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A picture of creatures capering in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges ANIMALS, and 'round' puts those letters around O to give MONALISA.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait of a smiling woman in the Louvre is perhaps the world's most famous painting.

clue.text: Open pub before start of evening

parts.note: a bar is a pub or a room in one

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of evening

explanation.surface: An instruction to unlock the pub before the evening begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means uncovered or exposed, the sense of open in 'open to the elements'.

clue.text: Mount Pleasant's end of day

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Mount Pleasant's end of day' (4) for PONY: 'Mount' defines PONY and 'end of day' gives Y, but no reading of 'Pleasant's' gives PON (PO for the Mount Pleasant sorting office leaves N unaccounted); likely OCR damage, and a search found no other print.

clue.text: Emperor's not one to embrace child without emotion

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps its arms round the child, holding it inside
not one means the emperor's word goes without one of its letters I

parts.note: imperial means belonging to an emperor
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a child

explanation.surface: The emperor is not a man to hug his child, being cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes one I from IMPERIAL to leave IMPERAL; 'to embrace' puts SON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done with no personal feeling or warmth is cold and detached.

clue.text: Exciting activity that turns out to be a gentle let-down?

definitions.text: Exciting activity that turns out to be a gentle let-down?

parts.words: Exciting activity that turns out to be a gentle let-down?
parts.note: a let-down is usually a disappointment, but here a thrilling leap from an aircraft literally ends with the jumper lowered gently to earth

explanation.surface: A thrilling hobby that proves an anticlimax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let-down' reads as disappointment; the canopy lets the jumper down gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap from an aircraft slowed by a canopy is both an adventurous sport and a slow descent.

clue.text: Home part represented — as nest, in one such?

definitions.text: Home part represented — as nest, in one such?

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters of home part are rearranged

explanation.surface: A domestic room depicted as a bird's nest in a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges HOME PART. The whole clue also defines: calling a home a nest is a figure of speech of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a home a nest describes one thing in terms of another, the figure of speech in question.

clue.text: What's shown on chart beside alien?

definitions.text: What's shown on chart beside alien?

indicators.note: the alien sits next to the chart word, so the pieces are joined side by side

parts.note: a plan is a chart or diagram
ET is the film extraterrestrial, a stock crossword alien

explanation.surface: Asking what appears on a star map next to a visitor from space.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: a world in space appears on an astrological chart, alongside alien life in fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrological and astronomical charts plot the positions of worlds orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Girl's set in gossip

indicators.note: the set word goes in the gossip word, inside it

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or gossip about a person
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: A young woman is the centre of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of anecdotes about someone, is a crossword staple for 'gossip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's given name, and crosswords define first names by 'girl'.

clue.text: Concern about newspaper restricting one's stance?

indicators.note: the concern word goes about the rest, wrapping it

parts.note: care means concern or worry

indicators.note: the newspaper word restricts, or confines, the one inside it

parts.note: a rag is slang for a poor newspaper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Worry over a tabloid limiting a person's position on an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' puts I inside RAG to give RIAG; 'about' puts CARE around that.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way one holds one's body, one's posture or bearing.

clue.text: I rant, turning in endless complaint about partying types?

indicators.note: the turned pieces go in the shortened complaint
endless means the complaint word loses its last letter

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble or complaint

indicators.note: turning means the word for rant is read backwards

parts.note: to rage is to rant

explanation.surface: Someone ranting at length in a complaint about party animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reads RAGE backwards as EGAR, and I follows; 'endless' cuts GROUSE to GROUS, and 'in' puts EGARI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregarious people love company, the sort for whom life is all about parties.

clue.text: One fellow in former co-operative is cast out

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the one and the fellow go in the co-operative word

parts.note: a commune is a co-operative community
I is the Roman numeral one
cat is jazz slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A member of an old collective is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT for 'fellow' is jazz-age slang, as in 'cool cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excommunicate is to expel someone from the church, banishing them.

clue.text: (Anything here would be inappropriate)

parts.note: the clue says that writing any clue in this space would be wrong, so the entry describes a place with no clue at all, a word that also means ignorant

explanation.surface: A bracketed remark that nothing should be said here.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank-looking clue is the joke: an entry meaning 'without a clue' can only properly have none.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any hint, and in slang lacking any idea, both describe being without guidance.

clue.text: Friend busy capturing sun's spectral section

indicators.note: the rearranged friend captures the sun god, holding him inside
busy letters are bustling about, so friend is rearranged

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A busy friend photographing part of the sun's spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges FRIEND, and 'capturing' puts RA inside to make INFRARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared is the band of radiation just beyond red in the spectrum.

clue.text: Wild slugger's brought about end of fight — this fight?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are brought about, around, the final letter
wild suggests the letters of slugger running out of control into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of fight

explanation.surface: A frenzied boxer has ended the bout in a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges SLUGGER, and 'brought about' puts it around T, the last letter of 'fight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle is a fight or tussle, such as a wild boxer's brawl.

clue.text: The upper classes attempt to follow information

indicators.note: the attempt word follows the information word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: Aristocrats try to keep up with the news.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen on something'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born landed class just below the nobility.

clue.text: In France drivers like a fight

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation
as means like, as in 'white as snow'

explanation.surface: French motorists getting into a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British drivers' association offering breakdown cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy brawl or disturbance.

clue.text: Notice opening at sea

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
a rift is a crack or opening

explanation.surface: An announcement of a gap at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift and at sea both mean drifting without direction, and also confused.

clue.text: Fur item, new, makes you hot

parts.note: a stole is a fur wrap worn round the shoulders

explanation.surface: A brand-new fur wrap keeps you warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is slang for stolen goods; the surface wants it to mean warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are hot are taken illegally, as in hot property.

clue.text: Mostly narrow strip of recording material

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: to taper is to narrow

explanation.surface: A thin band of recording stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts the last letter from TAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic tape is a long strip used to record sound or video.

clue.text: Brave, upright, initially and fair, possibly

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of upright
possibly suggests and with fair could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Describing someone courageous, honest from the start, and just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives U from 'upright'; 'possibly' rearranges AND FAIR into NAFRAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without fear is courageous, the same as being brave.

clue.text: Henry, left back, in a position indicative of possession?

indicators.note: the turned left and henry go in a position

parts.note: a pose is a position held, as for a portrait

indicators.note: back means the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
H is the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A footballer named Henry plays left back in a key position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PORT to TROP; with H that goes 'in' A POSE. Henry and left back hint at football.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark in 'Jack's' shows that something belongs to someone.

clue.text: Support losing Bible's quantity of gospels?

indicators.note: losing means the support word drops the Bible letters

parts.note: favour means support or backing
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Backing for scripture is falling, measured in gospels.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the Authorised (King James) Version, is a common crossword abbreviation for the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament has Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, a set of that many gospels.
